answer: In an agent freight market, each identity must lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before bidding to move walnut cargo from a jetty on an ocean voyage. The bond cannot back another identity while locked, so creating 1,000 eligible agents requires tying up $1 million. This does not prove the agents have different owners; it makes multiplying bidding identities costly in proportion to their number, even if creating accounts is free.
